reconstructed_theorem_text: Let X,A:[0,infinity)->R and T>=0. Suppose X and A are continuous on [0,T] and A has bounded variation on [0,T]. For t_i^n=i*T/2^n, i=0,...,2^n, the real sequence sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1} ( ((X+A)(t_{i+1}^n)-(X+A)(t_i^n))^2 - (X(t_{i+1}^n)-X(t_i^n))^2 ) tends to zero as n tends to infinity. No existence or convergence of the quadratic-variation sums of X is assumed. T=0 is allowed.
objects: Deterministic real functions X,A; horizon T; dyadic grid and difference of quadratic sums.
domains: Time NNReal, real function values, n natural, T nonnegative.
quantifiers: For every X,A,T, continuity of X,A and bounded variation of A on [0,T] imply the stated convergence.
assumptions: ContinuousOn X [0,T]; ContinuousOn A [0,T]; BoundedVariationOn A [0,T].
conclusion: The signed difference of the dyadic squared-increment sums for X+A and X tends to 0 in R.
scopes: Ordinary real convergence for a fixed horizon T, including zero; no stochastic or almost-everywhere claims.
constant_dependencies: No numerical bound or rate; sequence depends on X,A,T.
context_ambiguities: None identified from the supplied statement and definition context.
